approved: Customs Legislation Amendment (False Trade Marks Infringement Notices) Bill 2026

Moved that the Customs Legislation Amendment (False Trade Marks Infringement Notices) Bill 2026 be read a second time, proposing a strict liability offence and infringement notices for importing counterfeit goods, particularly commercial quantities of high-risk consumer products, to strengthen deterrence and protect consumers and Australian businesses.

Declared that the Customs Legislation Amendment (False Trade Marks Infringement Notices) Bill 2026 and Treasury Laws Amendment (Delivering an Efficient and Trusted Tax System) Bill 2026 stood referred to the Federation Chamber for further consideration.

Argued that the Customs Legislation Amendment (False Trade Marks Infringement Notices) Bill 2026 addresses counterfeit imports through a strict liability offence, financial penalties and Australian Border Force infringement powers, but raised concerns about proportionality, consultation and the absence of a clear trigger, and supported referral to a Senate inquiry.

Supported the Customs Legislation Amendment (False Trade Marks Infringement Notices) Bill 2026, arguing it would ease the burden on businesses and protect consumers from dangerous counterfeit goods, including medical devices, toys and chainsaws; the bill was read a second time and ordered to be reported without amendment.

Presented the fifth report of 2026 of the Selection of Bills Committee, recommending referrals of specified bills to parliamentary committees for inquiry and reporting by 30 April 2026, 5 May 2026, or 19 June 2026. Moved that the report be adopted, and the question was agreed to.

Moved the second reading of a bill creating a strict liability offence for importing goods with false trade marks and enabling infringement notices. The measure responds to over 700,000 counterfeit items seized in the 2024-25 financial year, supports enforcement by the Australian Border Force and aims to protect consumers and legitimate businesses.

Moved that government business, including five specified bills and a related bill subject to introduction, be considered from 12.15 pm until no later than 1.30 pm, followed by general business notice of motion no. 510 concerning the 2026-27 Budget. The question was agreed to.

Argued that the bill would create a strict liability offence for importing goods with false trademarks and allow Australian Border Force to issue infringement notices. Supported action against counterfeit goods but raised concerns about proportionality, personal imports, limited consultation and safeguards; the bill was ultimately supported and read a second time.
Customs Legislation Amendment (False Trade Marks Infringement Notices) Act 2026
